<module id="comparator_3bit">
    <description>Compare two 3-bit binary numbers A and B.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="A" width_description="[2:0]">First 3-bit input operand (binary number).</input>
        <input id="B" width_description="[2:0]">Second 3-bit input operand (binary number).</input>
        <output id="A_greater">1-bit output indicating if A is greater than B.</output>
        <output id="A_equal">1-bit output indicating if A is equal to B.</output>
        <output id="A_less">1-bit output indicating if A is less than B.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        // Comparison logic
        assign A_greater = (A > B);
        assign A_equal = (A == B);
        assign A_less = (A < B);
    </implementation>
</module>

module pe (
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input [31:0] a,
    input [31:0] b,
    output reg [31:0] c
);

always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
    if (rst) begin
        c <= 32'b0; 
    end else begin
        c <= c + (a * b); 
    end
end
endmodule

<module id="sub_64bit">
    <description>64-bit Subtractor with Overflow Checking</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="A" width_description="[63:0]">First 64-bit input operand (signed).</input>
        <input id="B" width_description="[63:0]">Second 64-bit input operand (signed).</input>
        <output id="result" width_description="[63:0]">Result of subtraction (signed).</output>
        <output id="overflow">Flag indicating overflow (1 for overflow, 0 otherwise).</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        // Perform subtraction
        assign result = A - B;
        
        // Check for overflow
        assign overflow = ((A[63] == 0 && B[63] == 1 && result[63] == 1) || (A[63] == 1 && B[63] == 0 && result[63] == 0)) ? 1 : 0;
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="multi_booth_8bit">
    <description>Radix-4 booth multiplier implementation.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="reset">Reset signal.</input>
        <input id="a" width_description="[7:0]">Multiplicand input.</input>
        <input id="b" width_description="[7:0]">Multiplier input.</input>
        <output id="p" width_description="[15:0]">Product output.</output>
        <output id="rdy">Ready signal.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        On the positive edge of the clock signal (clk) or the positive edge of the reset signal (reset), the module performs the multiplication process.
        If the reset signal (reset) is high, two 16-bit registers multiplier <= {{8{a[7]}}, a} and multiplicand <= {{8{b[7]}}, b}.
        If the reset signal (reset) is low, indicating normal operation, the module checks if the counter (5bit ctr) is less than 16.
        If the counter (ctr) is less than 16, the multiplicand register (multiplicand) is left-shifted by 1 to simulate the Booth algorithm's shifting operation.
        If the current bit of the multiplier register (multiplier[ctr]) is 1, indicating a positive Booth encoding, the product register (p) accumulates the value of the multiplicand register (multiplicand).
        The counter (ctr) is incremented by 1. Once the counter (ctr) reaches 16, indicating the completion of the multiplication process, the ready signal (rdy) is set to 1.
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="multi_16bit">
    <description>Implement an unsigned 16-bit multiplier using shift and accumulate operations.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Chip clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for chip reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="start">Chip enable signal to initiate the multiplication operation.</input>
        <input id="ain" width_description="[15:0]">Input signal representing the multiplicand (a) with a data width of 16 bits.</input>
        <input id="bin" width_description="[15:0]">Input signal representing the multiplier (b) with a data width of 16 bits.</input>
        <output id="yout" width_description="[31:0]">Product output signal with a data width of 32 bits.</output>
        <output id="done">Chip output flag signal. Defined as 1 indicates the completion of the multiplication operation.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="IDLE">State IDLE = 0.</parameter>
        <parameter id="START">State START = 1.</parameter>
        <parameter id="DONE">State DONE = 2.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <register id="i" type="shift_count_register">Shift count register initialized to 0.</register>
        <register id="done_r" type="multiplication_completion_flag">Multiplication completion flag initialized to 0.</register>
        <register id="areg" type="multiplicand_register">Multiplicand register initialized to 0.</register>
        <register id="breg" type="multiplier_register">Multiplier register initialized to 0.</register>
        <register id="yout_r" type="product_register">Product register initialized to 0.</register>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Shift Count Register Update Logic
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                i <= 0;
            end else if (start && i < 17) begin
                i <= i + 1;
            end else begin
                i <= 0;
            end
        end
        
        // Multiplication Completion Flag Generation Logic
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                done_r <= 0;
            end else if (i == 16) begin
                done_r <= 1;
            end else if (i == 17) begin
                done_r <= 0;
            end
        end
        
        // Shift and Accumulate Operation Logic
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                areg <= 0;
                breg <= 0;
                yout_r <= 0;
            end else if (start) begin
                if (i == 0) begin
                    areg <= ain;
                    breg <= bin;
                end else if (i > 0 && i < 17) begin
                    if (areg[i-1]) begin
                        yout_r <= yout_r + (breg << (i-1));
                    end
                end
            end
        end
        assign yout = yout_r;
        assign done = done_r;
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="fixed_point_subtractor">
    <description>A fixed-point subtractor for performing precise arithmetic operations with fixed precision.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="a" width_description="[N-1:0]">First N-bit fixed-point input operand.</input>
        <input id="b" width_description="[N-1:0]">Second N-bit fixed-point input operand.</input>
        <output id="c" width_description="[N-1:0]">N-bit output representing the result of the fixed-point subtraction.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="Q">Number of fractional bits in the fixed-point representation.</parameter>
        <parameter id="N">Total number of bits (integer + fractional) used for inputs and outputs.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <assign id="res" width_description="[N-1:0]">Result of the subtraction operation.</assign>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Different Sign Subtraction
        if (a[N-1] == b[N-1]) begin
            res = {a[N-1], a[N-2:0] - b[N-2:0]};
        end else begin
            // Same Sign Subtraction
            if ((a[N-1] == 1 && b[N-1] == 0) || (a[N-1] == 0 && b[N-1] == 1)) begin
                if (a > b) begin
                    res = {1'b0, a[N-2:0] + ~b[N-2:0] + 1};
                end else begin
                    res = {1'b1, ~(a[N-2:0] + ~b[N-2:0] + 1)};
                end
            end else begin
                // Handle Zero
                res = {1'b0, {(N-1){1'b0}}};
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

        <output id="result" width_description="[15:0]">Quotient output.</output>
        <output id="odd" width_description="[15:0]">Remainder output.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>Extracts the higher bits of the dividend, compares them with the divisor, sets the quotient to 1 if the dividend bits are greater, otherwise set it to 0, and uses the difference as the remainder.         <input id="valid_in">valid input</input>
        <input id="data_in" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit input data</input>
        <output id="valid_out">valid output</output>
        <output id="data_out" width_description="[15:0]">16-bit output data</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        // TODO: implement your solution here
        
        reg [15:0] data_out;
        reg [7:0] data_lock;
        reg flag;
        
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                data_out <= 0;
            end else begin
                if (flag && valid_in) begin
                    data_out <= {data_lock,data_in};
                end
            end

            if (!rst_n) begin

            if (!rst_n) begin
                data_lock <= 0;
            end else begin
                if (valid_in && !flag) begin
                    data_lock <= data_in;
                end
            end
        end

        assign data_out = data_out;

<module id="fixed_point_adder">
    <description>A parameterized fixed-point adder for arithmetic operations with fixed precision.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="a" width_description="[N-1:0]">First N-bit fixed-point input operand.</input>
        <input id="b" width_description="[N-1:0]">Second N-bit fixed-point input operand.</input>
        <output id="c" width_description="[N-1:0]">N-bit output representing the result of the fixed-point addition.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="Q">Number of fractional bits (precision).</parameter>
        <parameter id="N">Total number of bits, including integer and fractional parts.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <reg id="res" width_description="[N-1:0]">Register to store the result of the addition or subtraction.</reg>
        
        // Determine if the signs of 'a' and 'b' are the same
        <wire id="same_sign">((~a[N-1]) & (~b[N-1])) | ((a[N-1]) & (b[N-1]));</wire>
        
        // Calculate the absolute values of 'a' and 'b'
        <wire id="abs_a">a + {N{(~a[N-1])}};</wire>
        <wire id="abs_b">b + {N{(~b[N-1])}};</wire>
        
        // Perform absolute value addition if the signs are the same
        <assign id="abs_sum">abs_a + abs_b;</assign>
        
        // Perform absolute value subtraction if the signs are different
        <assign id="abs_diff">abs_a > abs_b ? abs_a - abs_b : abs_b - abs_a;</assign>
        
        // Assign the result based on the sign comparison
        <always @(*) begin
            if (same_sign) begin
                res = abs_sum;
                res[N-1] = a[N-1];
            end else begin
                res = abs_diff;
                res[N-1] = ~abs_diff[N-1];
            end
        end
        
        // Output assignment
        <assign id="c">res;</assign>
    </logic_description>
    
    <implementation>Fixed-point adder implementation with parameterization for precision and total bits.</implementation>
</module>

<module id="edge_detect">
    <description>Edge detector for detecting rising and falling edges of a 1-bit input signal 'a'.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="a">Input signal.</input>
        <output id="rise">Output signal indicating a rising edge.</output>
        <output id="down">Output signal indicating a falling edge.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        // Sequential logic block triggered on the positive edge of the clock or negative edge of reset
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                // On reset, initialize the previous value of 'a' to 0
                prev_a <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                // Update the previous value of 'a' with the current value of 'a'
                prev_a <= a;
            end
        end
        
        // Combinational logic to detect rising and falling edges
        assign rise = (prev_a == 1'b0 && a == 1'b1);
        assign down = (prev_a == 1'b1 && a == 1'b0);
    </implementation>
</module>

module fsm #(
    parameter s0 = 3'b000,
    parameter s1 = 3'b001,
    parameter s2 = 3'b010,
    parameter s3 = 3'b011,
    parameter s4 = 3'b100,
    parameter s5 = 3'b101
) (
    input IN,
    output reg MATCH,
    input CLK,
    input RST
);


reg [2:0] ST_cr;

always @(posedge CLK or posedge RST) begin
    if (RST) begin
        ST_cr <= s0;
    end else begin
        case (ST_cr)
            s0: begin
                if (IN == 1'b1) begin
                    ST_cr <= s1;
                end else begin
                    ST_cr <= s0;
                end
            end
            s1: begin
                if (IN == 1'b1) begin
                    ST_cr <= s1;
                end else begin
                    ST_cr <= s2;
                end
            end
            s2: begin
                if (IN == 1'b1) begin
                    ST_cr <= s1;
                end else begin
                    ST_cr <= s3;
                end
            end
            s3: begin
                if (IN == 1'b1) begin
                    ST_cr <= s4;
                end else begin
                    ST_cr <= s0;
                end
            end
            s4: begin
                if (IN == 1'b1) begin
                    ST_cr <= s5;
                end else begin
                    ST_cr <= s2;
                end
            end
            s5: begin
                if (IN == 1'b1) begin
                    ST_cr <= s1;
                end else begin
                    ST_cr <= s2;
                end
            end
            default: ST_cr <= s0;
        endcase
    end
end

always @(*) begin
    if (RST) begin
        MATCH = 0;
    end else if (ST_cr == s4 && IN == 1'b1) begin
        MATCH = 1;
    end else begin
        MATCH = 0;
    end
end

endmodule

<module id="fsm">
    <description>Mealy FSM detection circuit that detects a single-bit input IN. When the input is 10011, output MATCH is 1, and MATCH is 0 in other cases. Support for continuous input and loop detection.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="IN">Input signal to the FSM.</input>
        <input id="CLK">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="RST">Reset signal to initialize the FSM.</input>
        <output id="MATCH">Output signal indicating a match condition based on the FSM state.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="S0">Initial state.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S1">State after detecting '1'.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S2">State after detecting '10'.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S3">State after detecting '100'.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S4">State after detecting '1001'.</parameter>
        <parameter id="S5">State after detecting '10011'.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="current_state" width_description="[2:0]">Register to hold the current state of the FSM.</reg>
        <reg id="next_state" width_description="[2:0]">Register to hold the next state of the FSM.</reg>
        
        // State transition logic
        always @(posedge CLK or posedge RST) begin
            if (RST) begin
                current_state <= S0;
            end else begin
                current_state <= next_state;
            end
        end
        
        // Next state logic
        always @(*) begin
            case(current_state)
                S0: begin
                    if(IN == 1'b1) begin
                        next_state = S1;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = S0;
                    end
                end
                
                S1: begin
                    if(IN == 1'b0) begin
                        next_state = S2;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = S1;
                    end
                end
                
                S2: begin
                    if(IN == 1'b0) begin
                        next_state = S3;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = S1;
                    end
                end
                
                S3: begin
                    if(IN == 1'b1) begin
                        next_state = S4;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = S0;
                    end
                end
                
                S4: begin
                    if(IN == 1'b1) begin
                        next_state = S5;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = S0;
                    end
                end
                
                S5: begin
                    if(IN == 1'b0) begin
                        next_state = S2;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = S1;
                    end
                end
                
                default: next_state = S0;
            endcase
        end
        
        // Output logic
        assign MATCH = (current_state == S5 && IN == 1'b1);
    </logic_description>
    
    <implementation>Mealy FSM detection circuit that detects a single-bit input IN. When the input is 10011, output MATCH is 1, and MATCH is 0 in other cases. Support for continuous input and loop detection.</implementation>
</module>

<module id="signal_generator">
    <description>Triangle Wave Signal Generator</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <output id="wave" width_description="[4:0]">Generated waveform signal.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="0">Initial state.</parameter>
        <parameter id="1">Incrementing state.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="state" width_description="[1:0]">Register to store the current state.</reg>
        <reg id="wave" width_description="[4:0]">Register to store the generated waveform.</reg>
        
        // Sequential logic block triggered on positive edge of clk or negative edge of rst_n
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                // Reset condition: set state to 0 and wave to 0
                state <= 0;
                wave <= 0;
            end else begin
                // State machine to generate triangle wave pattern
                case(state)
                    0: begin
                        // Increment wave value by 1
                        wave <= wave + 1;
                        
                        // Check if wave has reached maximum value (31)
                        if(wave == 31) begin
                            // Transition to next state (incrementing state)
                            state <= 1;
                        end
                    end
                    
                    1: begin
                        // Decrement wave value by 1
                        wave <= wave - 1;
                        
                        // Check if wave has reached minimum value (0)
                        if(wave == 0) begin
                            // Transition back to initial state
                            state <= 0;
                        end
                    end
                endcase
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
    
    <implementation>Generates a triangular waveform by incrementing and decrementing the wave signal.</implementation>
</module>

<module id="multi_8bit">
    <description>Multiplies two 8-bit operands using shift-and-add method.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="A" width_description="[7:0]">First 8-bit input operand (multiplicand).</input>
        <input id="B" width_description="[7:0]">Second 8-bit input operand (multiplier).</input>
        <output id="product" width_description="[15:0]">16-bit output representing the product of the two 8-bit inputs (A * B).</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        // Internal variables
        integer i;
        reg [15:0] product_reg;
        reg [7:0] multiplicand;
        
        always @(*) begin
            product_reg = 0;
            multiplicand = A;
            
            for(i = 0; i < 8; i = i + 1) begin
                if(B[i] == 1'b1) begin
                    product_reg = product_reg + (multiplicand << i);
                end
            end
        end
        
        assign product = product_reg;
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="adder_bcd">
    <description>A 4-bit BCD adder for decimal arithmetic operations.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="A" width_description="[3:0]">First BCD input (4-bit).</input>
        <input id="B" width_description="[3:0]">Second BCD input (4-bit).</input>
        <input id="Cin">Carry-in input (1-bit).</input>
        <output id="Sum" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit output representing the sum of the two BCD inputs, corrected to be a valid BCD digit (0–9).</output>
        <output id="Cout">Carry-out output (1-bit), used when the sum exceeds the decimal value of 9.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        // Add A, B, and Cin
        wire [4:0] temp_sum;
        assign temp_sum = {1'b0, A} + {1'b0, B} + Cin;
        
        // Check if the sum exceeds 9 (1001 in binary)
        wire correction_needed;
        assign correction_needed = (temp_sum > 9);
        
        // Correct the sum if needed
        wire [4:0] corrected_sum;
        assign corrected_sum = correction_needed ? (temp_sum + 6) : temp_sum;
        
        // Assign outputs
        assign Sum = corrected_sum[3:0];
        assign Cout = corrected_sum[4];
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="traffic_light">
    <description>A traffic light system with red, yellow, green indicators and a pedestrian button.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="pass_request">Request signal for pedestrians to cross.</input>
        <output id="clock" width_description="[7:0]">Count value of the internal counter.</output>
        <output id="red">Red signal indicating the status of the traffic light.</output>
        <output id="yellow">Yellow signal indicating the status of the traffic light.</output>
        <output id="green">Green signal indicating the status of the traffic light.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="idle">Initial state.</parameter>
        <parameter id="s1_red">State after red signal.</parameter>
        <parameter id="s2_yellow">State after yellow signal.</parameter>
        <parameter id="s3_green">State after green signal.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <register id="cnt" width_description="[7:0]">Internal counter for timing control.</register>
        <register id="state" width_description="[1:0]">Current state of the traffic light controller.</register>
        <register id="p_red">Previous value of the red signal.</register>
        <register id="p_yellow">Previous value of the yellow signal.</register>
        <register id="p_green">Previous value of the green signal.</register>
        
        <always_comb>
            <case>
                <item value="idle">
                    <set id="state" value="s1_red"/>
                    <set id="p_red" value="0"/>
                    <set id="p_yellow" value="0"/>
                    <set id="p_green" value="0"/>
                </item>
                <item value="s1_red">
                    <if condition="cnt == 3">
                        <set id="state" value="s3_green"/>
                        <set id="p_red" value="0"/>
                        <set id="p_yellow" value="0"/>
                        <set id="p_green" value="1"/>
                    </if>
                    <else>
                        <set id="state" value="s1_red"/>
                        <set id="p_red" value="1"/>
                        <set id="p_yellow" value="0"/>
                        <set id="p_green" value="0"/>
                    </else>
                </item>
                <item value="s2_yellow">
                    <if condition="cnt == 3">
                        <set id="state" value="s1_red"/>
                        <set id="p_red" value="1"/>
                        <set id="p_yellow" value="0"/>
                        <set id="p_green" value="0"/>
                    </if>
                    <else>
                        <set id="state" value="s2_yellow"/>
                        <set id="p_red" value="0"/>
                        <set id="p_yellow" value="1"/>
                        <set id="p_green" value="0"/>
                    </else>
                </item>
                <item value="s3_green">
                    <if condition="cnt == 3">
                        <set id="state" value="s2_yellow"/>
                        <set id="p_red" value="0"/>
                        <set id="p_yellow" value="1"/>
                        <set id="p_green" value="0"/>
                    </if>
                    <else>
                        <set id="state" value="s3_green"/>
                        <set id="p_red" value="0"/>
                        <set id="p_yellow" value="0"/>
                        <set id="p_green" value="1"/>
                    </else>
                </item>
            </case>
        </always_comb>
        <always_comb>
            <if condition="!rst_n">
                <set id="cnt" value="10"/>
            </if>
            <else begin_if="pass_request && green">
                <set id="cnt" value="10"/>
            </else_begin_if>
            <else begin_else_if="!green && p_green">
                <set id="cnt" value="60"/>
            </else_begin_else_if>
            <else begin_else_if="!yellow && p_yellow">
                <set id="cnt" value="5"/>
            </else_begin_else_if>
            <else begin_else_if="!red && p_red">
                <set id="cnt" value="10"/>
            </else_begin_else_if>
            <else>
                <set id="cnt" value="cnt - 1"/>
            </else>
        </always_comb>
        <assign id="clock" value="cnt"/>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // State transition logic
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                state <= idle;
                p_red <= 0;
                p_yellow <= 0;
                p_green <= 0;
            end else begin
                case(state)
                    idle: begin
                        state <= s1_red;
                        p_red <= 0;
                        p_yellow <= 0;
                        p_green <= 0;
                    end
                    s1_red: begin
                        if(cnt == 3) begin
                            state <= s3_green;
                            p_red <= 0;
                            p_yellow <= 0;
                            p_green <= 1;
                        end else begin
                            state <= s1_red;
                            p_red <= 1;
                            p_yellow <= 0;
                            p_green <= 0;
                        end
                    end
                    s2_yellow: begin
                        if(cnt == 3) begin
                            state <= s1_red;
                            p_red <= 1;
                            p_yellow <= 0;
                            p_green <= 0;
                        end else begin
                            state <= s2_yellow;
                            p_red <= 0;
                            p_yellow <= 1;
                            p_green <= 0;
                        end
                    end
                    s3_green: begin
                        if(cnt == 3) begin
                            state <= s2_yellow;
                            p_red <= 0;
                            p_yellow <= 1;
                            p_green <= 0;
                        end else begin
                            state <= s3_green;
                            p_red <= 0;
                            p_yellow <= 0;
                            p_green <= 1;
                        end
                    end
                endcase
            end
        end
        
        // Counter logic
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                cnt <= 10;
            end else begin
                if(pass_request && green) begin
                    cnt <= 10;
                end else if(!green && p_green) begin
                    cnt <= 60;
                end else if(!yellow && p_yellow) begin
                    cnt <= 5;
                end else if(!red && p_red) begin
                    cnt <= 10;
                end else begin
                    cnt <= cnt - 1;
                end
            end
        end
        
        // Output assignment
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                red <= 0;
                yellow <= 0;
                green <= 0;
            end else begin
                red <= p_red;
                yellow <= p_yellow;
                green <= p_green;
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="parallel2serial">
    <description>Parallel to serial converter, converting 4 parallel inputs to 1 serial output.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="d" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit parallel data input.</input>
        <output id="valid_out">Valid signal indicating the availability of serial output.</output>
        <output id="dout">Serial output representing the converted data.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>Assigns the most significant bit of the parallel input to the serial output (dout). On each clock cycle, if the counter (cnt) is 3, indicating the last bit of the parallel input, the module updates the data register (data) with the parallel input (d), resets the counter (cnt) to 0, and sets the valid signal (valid) to 1. Otherwise, the module increments the counter (cnt) by 1, sets the valid signal (valid) to 0, and shifts the data register (data) one bit to the left, with the most significant bit shifted to the least significant bit. Counter Register: If the reset signal (rst_n) is high, the register (cnt) is incremented by 1.</implementation>
</module>

    <description>A ring counter is a type of sequential logic circuit used to generate cyclic state sequences. It consists of a series of flip-flops connected in a circular manner, where the output of one flip-flop feeds back into the input of the next. This creates a continuous cycle of states, allowing for efficient state transition and synchronization.</description>

        <input id="reset">Reset signal to initialize the counter to its starting state.</input>
        <output id="out" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit output representing the current state of the ring counter. Only one bit is set high at any time, and the set bit cycles through the 8-bit output.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>Initialize the counter to its starting state. On each rising edge of the clock signal, update the state based on the current state and the feedback mechanism. Handle the wrap-around condition to ensure the counter continues cycling through all possible states.</implementation>
</module>

<module id="multi_pipe_8bit">
    <description>Unsigned 8bit Multiplier using pipelined processing.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal. Defined as 0 for chip reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="mul_en_in">Input enable signal that controls the multiplication operation.</input>
        <input id="mul_a" width_description="[7:0]">Input signal representing the multiplicand with a data width of 8 bits.</input>
        <input id="mul_b" width_description="[7:0]">Input signal representing the multiplier with a data width of 8 bits.</input>
        <output id="mul_en_out">Output enable signal indicating if the multiplication operation is enabled.</output>
        <output id="mul_out" width_description="[15:0]">Product output signal with a data width of 16 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="IDLE">State IDLE = 0.</parameter>
        <parameter id="LOAD">State LOAD = 1.</parameter>
        <parameter id="CALCULATE">State CALCULATE = 2.</parameter>
        <parameter id="OUTPUT">State OUTPUT = 3.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="mul_en_out_reg" width_description="[3:0]">Register to hold the output enable signal.</reg>
        <reg id="mul_a_reg" width_description="[7:0]">Register to hold the multiplicand.</reg>
        <reg id="mul_b_reg" width_description="[7:0]">Register to hold the multiplier.</reg>
        <reg id="temp[0]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the first partial product.</reg>
        <reg id="temp[1]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the second partial product.</reg>
        <reg id="temp[2]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the third partial product.</reg>
        <reg id="temp[3]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the fourth partial product.</reg>
        <reg id="temp[4]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the fifth partial product.</reg>
        <reg id="temp[5]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the sixth partial product.</reg>
        <reg id="temp[6]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the seventh partial product.</reg>
        <reg id="temp[7]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the eighth partial product.</reg>
        <reg id="sum[0]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the first partial sum.</reg>
        <reg id="sum[1]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the second partial sum.</reg>
        <reg id="sum[2]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the third partial sum.</reg>
        <reg id="sum[3]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the fourth partial sum.</reg>
        <reg id="sum[4]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the fifth partial sum.</reg>
        <reg id="sum[5]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the sixth partial sum.</reg>
        <reg id="sum[6]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the seventh partial sum.</reg>
        <reg id="sum[7]" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the eighth partial sum.</reg>
        <reg id="mul_out_reg" width_description="[15:0]">Register to hold the final product.</reg>
        
        // Sequential logic block triggered on the positive edge of the clock signal
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            // Reset condition: When rst_n is low, initialize registers to zero
            if (!rst_n) begin
                mul_en_out_reg <= 4'd0;
                mul_a_reg <= 8'd0;
                mul_b_reg <= 8'd0;
                temp[0] <= 16'd0;
                temp[1] <= 16'd0;
                temp[2] <= 16'd0;
                temp[3] <= 16'd0;
                temp[4] <= 16'd0;
                temp[5] <= 16'd0;
                temp[6] <= 16'd0;
                temp[7] <= 16'd0;
                sum[0] <= 16'd0;
                sum[1] <= 16'd0;
                sum[2] <= 16'd0;
                sum[3] <= 16'd0;
                sum[4] <= 16'd0;
                sum[5] <= 16'd0;
                sum[6] <= 16'd0;
                sum[7] <= 16'd0;
                mul_out_reg <= 16'd0;
            end else begin
                // Update the output enable register with the input enable signal
                mul_en_out_reg <= {mul_en_out_reg[2:0], mul_en_in};
                
                // Update the multiplicand register with the input value when input enable is active
                if (mul_en_in) begin
                    mul_a_reg <= mul_a;
                end
                
                // Update the multiplier register with the input value when input enable is active
                if (mul_en_in) begin
                    mul_b_reg <= mul_b;
                end
                
                // Calculate the partial products based on the multiplier bits
                temp[0] <= mul_b_reg[0] ? {8'd0, mul_a_reg} : 16'd0;
                temp[1] <= mul_b_reg[1] ? {7'd0, mul_a_reg, 1'd0} : 16'd0;
                temp[2] <= mul_b_reg[2] ? {6'd0, mul_a_reg, 2'd0} : 16'd0;
                temp[3] <= mul_b_reg[3] ? {5'd0, mul_a_reg, 3'd0} : 16'd0;
                temp[4] <= mul_b_reg[4] ? {4'd0, mul_a_reg, 4'd0} : 16'd0;
                temp[5] <= mul_b_reg[5] ? {3'd0, mul_a_reg, 5'd0} : 16'd0;
                temp[6] <= mul_b_reg[6] ? {2'd0, mul_a_reg, 6'd0} : 16'd0;
                temp[7] <= mul_b_reg[7] ? {1'd0, mul_a_reg, 7'd0} : 16'd0;
                
                // Perform addition operations to calculate the partial sums
                sum[0] <= temp[0];
                sum[1] <= temp[1] + temp[0];
                sum[2] <= temp[2] + temp[1];
                sum[3] <= temp[3] + temp[2];
                sum[4] <= temp[4] + temp[3];
                sum[5] <= temp[5] + temp[4];
                sum[6] <= temp[6] + temp[5];
                sum[7] <= temp[7] + temp[6];
                
                // Accumulate the partial sums to get the final product
                mul_out_reg <= sum[0] + sum[1] + sum[2] + sum[3] + sum[4] + sum[5] + sum[6] + sum[7];
            end
        end
        
        // Assign the output product based on the output enable signal
        assign mul_out = mul_en_out_reg[3] ? mul_out_reg : 16'd0;
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>Implements an 8-bit unsigned multiplier using pipelined processing. The module has input and output ports for control signals, multiplicand, multiplier, and product output. Internal registers are used to store inputs and intermediate results during the multiplication process. Partial products are generated based on the multiplier bits, and partial sums are calculated through addition operations. Finally, the final product is obtained by accumulating all partial sums. The output product is assigned based on the output enable signal.</implementation>
</module>

<module id="freq_diveven">
    <description>Frequency divider that divides the input clock frequency by even numbers.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Input clock signal that will be divided.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal to initialize the module.</input>
        <output id="clk_div">Divided clock output signal.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="NUM_DIV">The division factor for the frequency divider, must be an even number.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="cnt" width_description="[3:0]">Counter to keep track of the number of clock cycles.</reg>
        <reg id="clk_div">Divided clock output signal.</reg>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Initialize the counter and divided clock signal
        cnt <= 0;
        clk_div <= 0;
        
        // Check if the reset signal is active
        if (~rst_n) begin
            // Reset the counter and divided clock signal
            cnt <= 0;
            clk_div <= 0;
        end else begin
            // Increment the counter on each positive edge of the input clock
            cnt <= cnt + 1;
            
            // Check if the counter has reached the specified division factor
            if (cnt == NUM_DIV/2 - 1) begin
                // Reset the counter and toggle the divided clock signal
                cnt <= 0;
                clk_div <= ~clk_div;
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="freq_div">
    <description>Frequency Divider for generating different clock frequencies based on input clock.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="CLK_in">Input clock signal.</input>
        <input id="RST">Reset signal.</input>
        <output id="CLK_50">Output clock signal with a frequency of CLK_in divided by 2.</output>
        <output id="CLK_10">Output clock signal with a frequency of CLK_in divided by 10.</output>
        <output id="CLK_1">Output clock signal with a frequency of CLK_in divided by 100.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        // Counter for CLK_50
        reg [0:0] cnt_50;
        always @(posedge CLK_in or posedge RST) begin
            if(RST) begin
                cnt_50 <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                cnt_50 <= ~cnt_50;
            end
        end
        
        // Counter for CLK_10
        reg [3:0] cnt_10;
        always @(posedge CLK_in or posedge RST) begin
            if(RST) begin
                cnt_10 <= 4'd0;
            end else if(cnt_10 == 4'd4) begin
                cnt_10 <= 4'd0;
            end else begin
                cnt_10 <= cnt_10 + 1;
            end
        end
        
        // Counter for CLK_1
        reg [6:0] cnt_100;
        always @(posedge CLK_in or posedge RST) begin
            if(RST) begin
                cnt_100 <= 7'd0;
            end else if(cnt_100 == 7'd49) begin
                cnt_100 <= 7'd0;
            end else begin
                cnt_100 <= cnt_100 + 1;
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

    <description>A barrel shifter for rotating bits efficiently. This 8-bit barrel shifter takes an 8-bit input and shifts or rotates the bits based on a 3-bit control signal.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="in" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit input to be shifted.</input>
        <input id="ctrl" width_description="[2:0]">3-bit control signal that determines how many positions to shift. The control signal specifies the amount of shift, where each bit indicates a shift by 1, 2, or 4 positions.</input>
        <output id="out" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit shifted output.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        // Define mux2X1 instances for different stages of the barrel shifter
        wire [7:0] mux2X1_stage0_out;
        wire [7:0] mux2X1_stage1_out;
        wire [7:0] mux2X1_stage2_out;
        
        // Instantiate the first stage of mux2X1s
        assign mux2X1_stage0_out = ctrl[2] ? {in[3:0], in[7:4]} : in;
        
        // Instantiate the second stage of mux2X1s
        assign mux2X1_stage1_out = ctrl[1] ? {mux2X1_stage0_out[5:0], mux2X1_stage0_out[7:6]} : mux2X1_stage0_out;
        
        // Instantiate the third stage of mux2X1s
        assign mux2X1_stage2_out = ctrl[0] ? {mux2X1_stage1_out[6:0], mux2X1_stage1_out[7]} : mux2X1_stage1_out;
        
        // Assign the final output of the barrel shifter
        assign out = mux2X1_stage2_out;
    </implementation>
</module>

module RAM (
    input clk,
    input rst_n,
    input write_en,
    input [7:0]write_addr,
    input [5:0]write_data,
    input read_en,
    input [7:0]read_addr,
    output reg [5:0]read_data
);

reg [5:0] RAM [2**8-1:0];

integer i;
initial begin
    for (i = 0; i < 2**8; i = i + 1) begin
        RAM[i] = 6'b000000;
    end
end

always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
        
        for (i = 0; i < 2**8; i = i + 1) begin
            RAM[i] <= 6'b000000;
        end
    end else if (write_en == 1) begin
        
        RAM[write_addr] <= write_data;
    end
end

always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
    if (!rst_n) begin
        
        read_data <= 6'b000000;
    end else if (read_en == 1) begin
        
        read_data <= RAM[read_addr];
    end else begin
        
        read_data <= 6'b000000;
    end
end
endmodule

<module id="RAM">
    <description>A dual-port RAM with a depth of 8 and a bit width of 6, initialized to 000000. Supports simultaneous read and write operations.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="write_en">Write enable signal for initiating write operations.</input>
        <input id="write_addr" width_description="[5:0]">Address for write operations.</input>
        <input id="write_data" width_description="[5:0]">Data to be written to the RAM.</input>
        <input id="read_en">Read enable signal for initiating read operations.</input>
        <input id="read_addr" width_description="[5:0]">Address for read operations.</input>
        <output id="read_data" width_description="[5:0]">Output data read from the RAM.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="WIDTH">6</parameter>
        <parameter id="DEPTH">8</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <reg id="read_data" width_description="[5:0]">Register to hold the read data.</reg>
        
        <always_comb>
            if (!rst_n) begin
                read_data <= 6'b000000;
            end else if (read_en == 1) begin
                read_data <= RAM[read_addr];
            end else begin
                read_data <= 6'b000000;
            end
        </always_comb>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Define the RAM array
        reg [DEPTH - 1 : 0] RAM [2**WIDTH-1:0]; 
        
        // Initialize the RAM contents to 000000
        integer i;
        initial begin
            for (i = 0; i < 2**WIDTH; i = i + 1) begin
                RAM[i] = 6'b000000;
            end
        end
        
        // Sequential logic for writing data to the RAM
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                // Reset the RAM contents to 000000
                for (i = 0; i < 2**WIDTH; i = i + 1) begin
                    RAM[i] <= 6'b000000;
                end
            end else if (write_en == 1) begin
                // Write data to the RAM at the specified address
                RAM[write_addr] <= write_data;
            end
        end
        
        // Sequential logic for reading data from the RAM
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                // Reset the read_data register to 000000
                read_data <= 6'b000000;
            end else if (read_en == 1) begin
                // Read data from the RAM at the specified address
                read_data <= RAM[read_addr];
            end else begin
                // Clear the read_data register if read_en is not active
                read_data <= 6'b000000;
            end
        end
    </implementation>
    
</module>

<module id="comparator_4bit">
    <description>Comparator for 4-bit binary numbers.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="A" width_description="[3:0]">First 4-bit input operand.</input>
        <input id="B" width_description="[3:0]">Second 4-bit input operand.</input>
        <output id="A_greater">Output indicating if A is greater than B.</output>
        <output id="A_equal">Output indicating if A is equal to B.</output>
        <output id="A_less">Output indicating if A is less than B.</output>
    </ports>
    
    <parameter_description>
        <!-- No parameter descriptions needed -->
    </parameter_description>
    
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        // Internal signals for subtraction results
        wire [3:0] subtract_result;
        wire [3:0] borrow;
        
        // Full Adder for each bit position
        assign subtract_result[0] = A[0] ^ B[0];          // XOR for first bit comparison
        assign borrow[0] = ~A[0] & B[0];                   // Borrow generation
        
        assign subtract_result[1] = (A[1] ^ B[1]) ^ borrow[0];      // XOR for second bit comparison
        assign borrow[1] = (~A[1] & B[1]) | ((~A[1] | B[1]) & borrow[0]);  // Borrow generation
        
        assign subtract_result[2] = (A[2] ^ B[2]) ^ borrow[1];      // XOR for third bit comparison
        assign borrow[2] = (~A[2] & B[2]) | ((~A[2] | B[2]) & borrow[1]);  // Borrow generation
        
        assign subtract_result[3] = (A[3] ^ B[3]) ^ borrow[2];      // XOR for fourth bit comparison
        assign borrow[3] = (~A[3] & B[3]) | ((~A[3] | B[3]) & borrow[2]);  // Borrow generation
        
        // Final comparisons based on the borrow values
        assign A_less = borrow[3];
        assign A_greater = (subtract_result != 4'd0 && !borrow[3]);
        assign A_equal = (subtract_result == 4'd0);
    </logic_description>
    
    <implementation>Combination of 4 1-bit comparators to perform 4-bit comparison using full adders and subtraction logic.</implementation>
    
</module>

<module id="synchronizer">
    <description>A multi-bit MUX-based synchronizer. Data remains constant during the period when data_en is high, and data_en is high for at least 3 clk_b clock cycles. When the value of data_en is high, data can be synchronized. The data change frequency of data_in is very low. The change interval between two adjacent data is at least 10 clk_b clock cycles.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk_a">Clock signal A used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="clk_b">Clock signal B used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="arstn">Active-low reset signal A. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="brstn">Active-low reset signal B. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="data_in" width_description="[3:0]">Input data signal of size 4 bits.</input>
        <input id="data_en">Input enable signal that controls the selection operation.</input>
        <output id="dataout" width_description="[3:0]">Output data signal of size 4 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        // Data Register
        reg [3:0] data_reg;
        always @(posedge clk_a or negedge arstn) begin
            if (~arstn) begin
                data_reg <= 4'd0;
            end else begin
                data_reg <= data_in;
            end
        end
        
        // Enable Data Register
        reg en_data_reg;
        always @(posedge clk_a or negedge arstn) begin
            if (~arstn) begin
                en_data_reg <= 1'd0;
            end else begin
                en_data_reg <= data_en;
            end
        end
        
        // Enable Control Registers
        reg en_clap_one;
        reg en_clap_two;
        
        always @(posedge clk_b or negedge brstn) begin
            if (~brstn) begin
                en_clap_one <= 1'd0;
                en_clap_two <= 1'd0;
            end else begin
                en_clap_one <= en_data_reg;
                en_clap_two <= en_clap_one;
            end
        end
        
        // Output Assignment
        reg [3:0] dataout;
        always @(posedge clk_b or negedge brstn) begin
            if (~brstn) begin
                dataout <= 4'd0;
            end else begin
                if (en_clap_two) begin
                    dataout <= data_reg;
                end else begin
                    dataout <= dataout;
                end
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="freq_divbyodd">
    <description>A frequency divider that divides the input clock frequency by odd numbers. The module generates a divided clock output by an odd divisor value provided as a parameter.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Input clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Active low reset signal that initializes the divider.</input>
        <output id="clk_div">Divided clock output.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="NUM_DIV" value="5">Odd divisor value for frequency division.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        <signal id="cnt1_next" width_description="[3:0]">Next value for counter 1.</signal>
        <signal id="cnt2_next" width_description="[3:0]">Next value for counter 2.</signal>
        <signal id="clk_div1_next">Next value for clock divider 1.</signal>
        <signal id="clk_div2_next">Next value for clock divider 2.</signal>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Counter 1 for rising edge detection
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                cnt1 <= 4'd0;
            end else begin
                cnt1 <= cnt1_next;
            end
        end
        
        // Counter 2 for falling edge detection
        always @(negedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                cnt2 <= 4'd0;
            end else begin
                cnt2 <= cnt2_next;
            end
        end
        
        // Clock divider 1 for rising edge
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                clk_div1 <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                clk_div1 <= clk_div1_next;
            end
        end
        
        // Clock divider 2 for falling edge
        always @(negedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (~rst_n) begin
                clk_div2 <= 1'b0;
            end else begin
                clk_div2 <= clk_div2_next;
            end
        end
        
        // Combinational logic for next values
        assign cnt1_next = (cnt1 == (NUM_DIV/2)) ? 4'd0 : cnt1 + 4'd1;
        assign cnt2_next = (cnt2 == (NUM_DIV/2)) ? 4'd0 : cnt2 + 4'd1;
        
        assign clk_div1_next = (cnt1 >= (NUM_DIV/2)) ? ~clk_div1 : clk_div1;
        assign clk_div2_next = (cnt2 >= (NUM_DIV/2)) ? ~clk_div2 : clk_div2;
        
        // Final divided clock output
        assign clk_div = clk_div1 | clk_div2;
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="LIFObuffer">
    <description>A Last-In-First-Out (LIFO) buffer for temporary data storage. This 4-bit wide buffer can hold up to 4 entries, allowing for push and pop operations controlled by read/write (RW) signals.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="dataIn" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit input data to be pushed onto the buffer.</input>
        <input id="RW">Read/Write control signal (1 for read, 0 for write).</input>
        <input id="EN">Enable signal to activate buffer operations.</input>
        <input id="Rst">Active high reset signal to initialize the buffer.</input>
        <input id="Clk">Clock signal for synchronous operations.</input>
        <output id="EMPTY">Flag indicating whether the buffer is empty.</output>
        <output id="FULL">Flag indicating whether the buffer is full.</output>
        <output id="dataOut" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit output data retrieved from the buffer.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        // Stack memory declaration
        reg [3:0] stack_mem[0:3];
        
        // Stack pointer initialization
        integer SP = 4;
        
        // Output assignment
        assign EMPTY = (SP == 4);
        assign FULL = (SP == 0);
        assign dataOut = stack_mem[SP];
        
        // Sequential logic block triggered on the positive edge of the clock
        always @(posedge Clk) begin
            if (EN) begin
                if (Rst) begin
                    // Resetting the stack memory and stack pointer
                    SP <= 4;
                    stack_mem[0] <= 4'd0;
                    stack_mem[1] <= 4'd0;
                    stack_mem[2] <= 4'd0;
                    stack_mem[3] <= 4'd0;
                end else begin
                    // Write operation
                    if (!RW && !FULL) begin
                        stack_mem[SP] <= dataIn;
                        SP <= SP - 1;
                    end
                    
                    // Read operation
                    else if (RW && !EMPTY) begin
                        SP <= SP + 1;
                        stack_mem[SP] <= 4'd0;
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="pulse_detect">
    <description>Implements a pulse detector that detects transitions from 0 to 1 to 0 (three cycles).</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="data_in">One-bit input signal.</input>
        <output id="data_out">Output signal indicating the presence of pulses.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="INITIAL_STATE">Initial state of the pulse detector.</parameter>
        <parameter id="PULSE_STATE">State representing the detected pulse.</parameter>
        <parameter id="WAITING_STATE">Waiting state after detecting a pulse.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <register id="state" width_description="[2:0]">Register to hold the current state of the pulse detector.</register>
        <register id="next_state" width_description="[2:0]">Register to hold the next state of the pulse detector.</register>
        
        <always @(*) begin
            case(state)
                INITIAL_STATE: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b1) begin
                        next_state = PULSE_STATE;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = INITIAL_STATE;
                    end
                end
                
                PULSE_STATE: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b0) begin
                        next_state = WAITING_STATE;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = PULSE_STATE;
                    end
                end
                
                WAITING_STATE: begin
                    if(data_in == 1'b0) begin
                        next_state = INITIAL_STATE;
                    end else begin
                        next_state = WAITING_STATE;
                    end
                end
                
                default: next_state = INITIAL_STATE;
            endcase
        end
        
        <always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if(~rst_n) begin
                state <= INITIAL_STATE;
            end else begin
                state <= next_state;
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
    
    <implementation>
        Always block sensitive to the positive edge of clk and negative edge of rst_n.
        Inside the always block, use a case statement to handle different states of the pulse detector.
        In the INITIAL_STATE, check the value of data_in. If it's 1, move to the PULSE_STATE. Otherwise, remain in the INITIAL_STATE.
        In the PULSE_STATE, check the value of data_in. If it's 0, move to the WAITING_STATE. Otherwise, remain in the PULSE_STATE.
        In the WAITING_STATE, check the value of data_in. If it's 0, return to the INITIAL_STATE. Otherwise, remain in the WAITING_STATE.
        Default case: set state to INITIAL_STATE.
        
        Sequential logic to update the state register based on the next_state register.
        Use non-blocking assignment to update state in the positive edge of clk.
        Set data_out to 1 if the current state is PULSE_STATE and data_in is 1, otherwise set it to 0.
    </implementation>
</module>

                end
            end

                state <= IDLE;
            end

<module id="sequence_detector">
    <description>A 4-bit sequence detector to detect the sequence '1001'.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">The clock signal for synchronization.</input>
        <input id="reset_n">The active-low reset signal.</input>
        <input id="data_in">A 1-bit input data stream.</input>
        <output id="sequence_detected">A 1-bit output indicating if the sequence was detected.</output>
    </ports>
    <implementation>
        <parameter_description>
            <parameter name="IDLE">Waiting for the start of the sequence.</parameter>
            <parameter name="S1">Detected the first bit of the sequence.</parameter>
            <parameter name="S2">Detected the second bit of the sequence.</parameter>
            <parameter name="S3">Detected the third bit of the sequence.</parameter>
            <parameter name="S4">Detected the fourth bit of the sequence.</parameter>
        </parameter_description>
        
        // Declare state register
        reg [2:0] current_state;
        
        // Sequential logic block triggered on the rising edge of the clock or the negative edge of reset
        always @(posedge clk or negedge reset_n) begin
            // Check for the negative edge of reset to return to initial state
            if (!reset_n) begin
                current_state <= 3'd0;  // Reset the state to IDLE (000)
            end else begin
                case(current_state)
                    // Default case to handle unexpected states
                    default: current_state <= 3'd0;  // Set to IDLE state
                    // Transition rules for each state
                    3'd0: current_state <= data_in ? 3'd1 : 3'd0;  // S1 = 001 if data_in is 1, otherwise stay in IDLE
                    3'd1: current_state <= ~data_in ? 3'd2 : 3'd0;  // S2 = 010 if data_in is 0, otherwise go back to IDLE
                    3'd2: current_state <= data_in ? 3'd3 : 3'd0;  // S3 = 011 if data_in is 1, otherwise go back to IDLE
                    3'd3: current_state <= ~data_in ? 3'd4 : 3'd0;  // S4 = 100 if data_in is 0, otherwise go back to IDLE
                    3'd4: current_state <= 3'd0;  // Stay in S4 after detecting the last bit
                endcase
            end
        end
        
        // Combinational logic to assert the output signal based on the current state
        assign sequence_detected = (current_state == 3'd4);
    </implementation>
</module>

);

module dual_port_RAM #(parameter DEPTH = 16,  parameter WIDTH = 8)
(
	 input wclk	,
	 input wenc	,
	 input [$clog2(DEPTH)-1:0] waddr  ,
	 input [WIDTH-1:0] wdata ,
	 input rclk	,
	 input renc	,
	 input [$clog2(DEPTH)-1:0] raddr ,
	 output reg [WIDTH-1:0] rdata 		
);

	if(wenc)
		RAM_MEM[waddr] <= wdata;
end 

always @(posedge rclk) begin
	if(renc)
		rdata <= RAM_MEM[raddr];
end 

endmodule

<module id="asyn_fifo">
    <description>An asynchronous FIFO implemented using a dual-port RAM module, with separate write and read controllers, and synchronized read and write pointers.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="wclk">Write clock signal used for synchronous write operations.</input>
        <input id="rclk">Read clock signal used for synchronous read operations.</input>
        <input id="wrstn">Write reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="rrstn">Read reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="winc">Write increment signal. Used to trigger write operations.</input>
        <input id="rinc">Read increment signal. Used to trigger read operations.</input>
        <input id="wdata" width_description="[WIDTH-1:0]">Write data input. The width [WIDTH-1:0] is configurable and represents the data to be written into the FIFO.</input>
        <output id="wfull">Write full signal. Indicates if the FIFO is full and cannot accept further write operations.</output>
        <output id="rempty">Read empty signal. Indicates if the FIFO is empty and cannot provide any data for read operations.</output>
        <output id="rdata" width_description="[WIDTH-1:0]">Read data output. The width [WIDTH-1:0] is configurable and represents the data read from the FIFO.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="WIDTH" value="8">FIFO data width configuration parameter.</parameter>
        <parameter id="DEPTH" value="16">FIFO depth configuration parameter.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="combinational_logic">
        // Define parameters
        parameter ADDR_WIDTH = $clog2(DEPTH);
        parameter DATA_WIDTH = WIDTH;
        
        // Declare internal signals
        reg [ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] waddr_bin, raddr_bin;
        reg [DATA_WIDTH-1:0] wdata_reg;
        reg wen, ren;
        reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wptr, rptr;
        reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wptr_buff, rptr_buff;
        reg [ADDR_WIDTH:0] wptr_syn, rptr_syn;
        reg wfull_reg, rempty_reg;
        
        // Connect input/output signals to RAM module
        assign wen = winc & !wfull_reg;
        assign ren = rinc & !rempty_reg;
        assign wdata_reg = wdata;
        assign rdata = ren ? wdata_reg : {DATA_WIDTH{1'bz}};
        
        // Write pointer management
        always @(posedge wclk or negedge wrstn) begin
            if (!wrstn) begin
                waddr_bin <= 0;
                wptr <= 0;
            end else begin
                if (wen) begin
                    waddr_bin <= waddr_bin + 1;
                    wptr <= wptr ^ (wptr >> 1);
                end
            end
        end
        
        // Read pointer management
        always @(posedge rclk or negedge rrstn) begin
            if (!rrstn) begin
                raddr_bin <= 0;
                rptr <= 0;
            end else begin
                if (ren) begin
                    raddr_bin <= raddr_bin + 1;
                    rptr <= rptr ^ (rptr >> 1);
                end
            end
        end
        
        // Gray code conversion
        function [ADDR_WIDTH:0] bin_to_gray(input [ADDR_WIDTH:0] bin);
            integer i;
            begin
                bin_to_gray[ADDR_WIDTH] = bin[ADDR_WIDTH];
                for (i = ADDR_WIDTH-1; i >= 0; i = i - 1) begin
                    bin_to_gray[i] = bin[i+1] ^ bin[i];
                end
            end
        endfunction
        
        // Pointer synchronization
        always @(posedge wclk or negedge wrstn) begin
            if (!wrstn) begin
                wptr_buff <= 0;
            end else begin
                wptr_buff <= wptr;
            end
        end
        
        always @(posedge rclk or negedge rrstn) begin
            if (!rrstn) begin
                rptr_buff <= 0;
            end else begin
                rptr_buff <= rptr;
            end
        end
        
        // Full and empty signal generation
        always @(*) begin
            if (wptr == ~rptr_syn || (wptr[ADDR_WIDTH] != rptr_syn[ADDR_WIDTH] && wptr[ADDR_WIDTH-1:0] == rptr_syn[ADDR_WIDTH-1:0])) begin
                wfull_reg = 1;
            end else begin
                wfull_reg = 0;
            end
            
            if (rptr == wptr_syn) begin
                rempty_reg = 1;
            end else begin
                rempty_reg = 0;
            end
        end
        
        // Assign outputs
        assign wfull = wfull_reg;
        assign rempty = rempty_reg;
        
        // Synchronize read pointer
        always @(posedge wclk or negedge wrstn) begin
            if (!wrstn) begin
                rptr_syn <= 0;
            end else begin
                rptr_syn <= rptr_buff;
            end
        end
        
        // Synchronize write pointer
        always @(posedge rclk or negedge rrstn) begin
            if (!rrstn) begin
                wptr_syn <= 0;
            end else begin
                wptr_syn <= wptr_buff;
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Dual-port RAM instance
        dual_port_RAM #( .depth(DEPTH), .width(DATA_WIDTH)) ram_inst (
            .wclk(wclk),
            .wenc(wen),
            .waddr(waddr_bin),
            .wdata(wdata_reg),
            .rclk(rclk),
            .renc(ren),
            .raddr(raddr_bin),
            .rdata(rdata)
        );
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="radix2_div">
    <description>A simplified radix-2 divider for 8-bit signed or unsigned integers.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">The clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst">The reset signal to initialize or reset the module.</input>
        <input id="sign">Indicates if the operation is signed (1) or unsigned (0).</input>
        <input id="dividend" width_description="[7:0]">The 8-bit input signal representing the dividend for division.</input>
        <input id="divisor" width_description="[7:0]">The 8-bit input signal representing the divisor for division.</input>
        <input id="opn_valid">A 1-bit input signal indicating that a valid operation request is present.</input>
        <output id="res_valid">A 1-bit output signal indicating the result is valid and ready.</output>
        <output id="result" width_description="[15:0]">The 16-bit output containing the remainder in the upper 8 bits and the quotient in the lower 8 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="DIVIDE">1'b0</parameter>
        <parameter id="IDLE">1'b1</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="state" type="enum" values="DIVIDE,IDLE">The current state of the divider.</reg>
        <reg id="next_state" type="enum" values="DIVIDE,IDLE">The next state of the divider.</reg>
        <reg id="start_cnt">Flag to indicate the start of the division process.</reg>
        <reg id="res_valid_reg">Register to hold the result validity flag.</reg>
        <reg id="neg_sign">Flag to indicate negative sign.</reg>
        <reg id="cnt">Counter for the division process.</reg>
        <wire id="carry_out">Wire to hold the carry-out value.</wire>
        <wire id="sub_result">Wire to hold the subtraction result.</wire>
        <wire id="mux_out">Wire to hold the MUX output.</wire>
        <reg id="remainder">Register to hold the remainder value.</reg>
        <reg id="quotient">Register to hold the quotient value.</reg>
        <reg id="SR">Shift Register to store the dividend during the division process.</reg>
        <reg id="NEG_DIVISOR">Register to hold the negative value of the divisor.</reg>
        
        // Sequential Logic Block
        always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
            if (rst) begin
                state <= IDLE;
                res_valid_reg <= 1'b0;
                cnt <= 1'b0;
                start_cnt <= 1'b0;
                SR <= 16'b0;
                NEG_DIVISOR <= 16'b0;
                remainder <= 8'b0;
                quotient <= 8'b0;
            end else begin
                case(state)
                    DIVIDE: begin
                        if(cnt[3]) begin
                            cnt <= 1'b0;
                            start_cnt <= 1'b0;
                            SR <= {remainder, quotient};
                            state <= IDLE;
                        end else begin
                            cnt <= cnt + 1'b1;
                            start_cnt <= 1'b1;
                            SR <= {mux_out, SR[7:1]};
                        end
                    end
                    
                    IDLE: begin
                        if(opn_valid && !res_valid_reg) begin
                            state <= DIVIDE;
                            cnt <= 1'b1;
                            start_cnt <= 1'b1;
                            SR <= {8'h00, dividend} << 1;
                            NEG_DIVISOR <= (~{1'b0, divisor}) + 1'b1;
                        end
                    end
                endcase
            end
        end
        
        // Combinational Logic Block
        always @(*) begin
            if(start_cnt) begin
                {carry_out, sub_result} = SR[8:0] + NEG_DIVISOR;
                mux_out = (carry_out == 1'b1) ? sub_result : SR[8];
                if(carry_out == 1'b1) begin
                    remainder = sub_result;
                    quotient[cnt-1] = 1'b0;
                end else begin
                    remainder = SR[8:0];
                    quotient[cnt-1] = 1'b1;
                end
            end else begin
                remainder = 8'b0;
                quotient = 8'b0;
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        The module implements a simplified radix-2 divider for 8-bit signed or unsigned integers. It handles both signed and unsigned division operations. The module uses a sequential logic block to manage the division process and a combinational logic block to perform the actual division calculations. The division process starts when opn_valid is high and res_valid is low. The module saves the inputs dividend and divisor, initializes the shift register SR with the absolute value of the dividend shifted left by one bit, sets NEG_DIVISOR to the negated absolute value of the divisor, and sets the counter cnt to 1 and start_cnt to 1 to begin the division process. If start_cnt is high, the module performs the following steps: If the counter cnt reaches 8 (most significant bit of cnt is set), the division is complete: cnt and start_cnt are cleared. Updates the shift register SR with the final remainder and quotient. Otherwise, the counter cnt is incremented, and the shift register SR is updated based on the subtraction result: Computes the subtraction of NEG_DIVISOR. Uses a multiplexer to select the appropriate result based on the carry-out. Updates SR by shifting left and inserting the carry-out. The result validity flag res_valid is managed based on the reset signal, the counter, and whether the result has been consumed.
    </implementation>
</module>

<module id="float_multi">
    <description>Multiplies two 32-bit IEEE 754 floating point numbers.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst">Reset signal.</input>
        <input id="a" width_description="[31:0]">First operand.</input>
        <input id="b" width_description="[31:0]">Second operand.</input>
        <output id="z" width_description="[31:0]">Result of multiplication.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="INIT">Initial state.</parameter>
        <parameter id="INPUT">State after extracting operands.</parameter>
        <parameter id="SPECIAL_CASES">State for handling special cases.</parameter>
        <parameter id="NORMALIZE">State for normalizing mantissas.</parameter>
        <parameter id="MULTIPLY">State for performing multiplication.</parameter>
        <parameter id="ROUND">State for rounding the result.</parameter>
        <parameter id="OUTPUT">Final output state.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <signal id="counter" type="reg" width="3">Cycle counter.</signal>
        <signal id="a_mantissa" type="reg" width="24">Mantissa of input 'a'.</signal>
        <signal id="b_mantissa" type="reg" width="24">Mantissa of input 'b'.</signal>
        <signal id="z_mantissa" type="reg" width="24">Mantissa of output 'z'.</signal>
        <signal id="a_exponent" type="reg" width="10">Exponent of input 'a'.</signal>
        <signal id="b_exponent" type="reg" width="10">Exponent of input 'b'.</signal>
        <signal id="z_exponent" type="reg" width="10">Exponent of output 'z'.</signal>
        <signal id="a_sign" type="reg">Sign bit of input 'a'.</signal>
        <signal id="b_sign" type="reg">Sign bit of input 'b'.</signal>
        <signal id="z_sign" type="reg">Sign bit of output 'z'.</signal>
        <signal id="product" type="reg" width="50">Product of mantissas.</signal>
        <signal id="guard_bit" type="reg">Guard bit for rounding.</signal>
        <signal id="round_bit" type="reg">Round bit for rounding.</signal>
        <signal id="sticky" type="reg">Sticky bit for rounding.</signal>
        
        <always @(posedge clk or posedge rst)>
            if (rst) begin
                counter <= 3'd0;
            end else begin
                case(counter)
                    INIT: begin
                        // Extract mantissas, exponents, and sign bits
                        a_mantissa <= {1'b1, a[22:0]};
                        b_mantissa <= {1'b1, b[22:0]};
                        a_exponent <= a[30:23];
                        b_exponent <= b[30:23];
                        a_sign <= a[31];
                        b_sign <= b[31];
                        
                        // Initialize other variables
                        z_mantissa <= 24'd0;
                        z_exponent <= 10'd0;
                        z_sign <= 1'b0;
                        product <= 50'd0;

<module id="serial2parallel">
    <description>Serial-to-Parallel Conversion Circuit</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal (active low).</input>
        <input id="din_serial">Serial input data.</input>
        <input id="din_valid">Validity signal for input data.</input>
        <output id="dout_parallel" width_description="[7:0]">Parallel output data (8 bits wide).</output>
        <output id="dout_valid">Validity signal for the output data.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="COUNTER_WIDTH">4</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="cnt" width_description="[COUNTER_WIDTH-1:0]">Counter to keep track of the number of serial input data bits received.</reg>
        <reg id="dout_parallel" width_description="[7:0]">Parallel output data register.</reg>
        <reg id="dout_valid">Valid output signal register.</reg>
        
        // Sequential logic block triggered on the positive edge of clk
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                cnt <= 0;
                dout_parallel <= 0;
                dout_valid <= 0;
            end else begin
                if (din_valid) begin
                    dout_parallel[cnt] <= din_serial;
                    cnt <= cnt + 1;
                    
                    // Check if all 8 serial data bits have been received
                    if (cnt == 7) begin
                        dout_valid <= 1;
                        cnt <= 0; // Reset the counter after processing 8 bits
                    end else begin
                        dout_valid <= 0;
                    end
                end
            end
        end
    </logic_description>
</module>
